summary: The post-EASD 2026 (European diabetes congress) wave has moved from conference abstracts to peer-reviewed papers and mainstream coverage. The best early openings name a specific drug, and some of the newest results are mixed, so we can explain them honestly. 1) Survodutide in adults with type 2 diabetes (SYNCHRONIZE-2, NEJM Oct 1): 13.1% vs 3.1% weight loss at 76 weeks, and STAT called it a "disappointment". 2) Orforglipron (Foundayo) heart-safety trial vs insulin glargine (ACHIEVE-4, Lancet). 3) Trevogrumab, an experimental antibody, cut lean-mass loss on semaglutide to 4.2% vs 7.3% over a year (Phase 2, company release, not yet peer-reviewed). 4) Petrelintide, an amylin drug (ZUPREME-1, Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology), alongside CNBC's "amylin is next" story. 5) A UK study of 47,039 patients found regurgitation or aspiration under anaesthesia in 1.41% of GLP-1 users vs 0.12% of non-users. Retatrutide's TRIUMPH-2 is now in The Lancet. Its new searchable number is 23.4% average weight loss at 80 weeks in people with a BMI of 35 or more, but coverage is close to peaking, so it needs a decoder angle. Nail and hair loss, the postpartum prescribing surge (JAMA) and semaglutide for alcohol use are being picked up by mainstream outlets. Topics from earlier snapshots are cooling: stopping GLP-1s ("metabolic whiplash"), SELECT mediation, and pancreatic cancer. Rejected: GLP-1 "microdosing" content and the political naming story. I left out the online-seller story because it risks pointing people to sources. Every title should name the drug and its comparator, as our analytics suggest.

candidates.topic: Survodutide (Boehringer/Zealand) in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes: 13.1% vs 3.1% placebo weight loss at 76 weeks (SYNCHRONIZE-2, NEJM, Oct 1 2026)
candidates.angle: Headline decoder: 'Did survodutide disappoint?' Put 13.1% (6 mg) and 10.4% (3.6 mg) vs 3.1% placebo next to how type 2 diabetes usually blunts weight loss on every GLP-1. Explain glucagon + GLP-1 dual action and why it's being studied for fatty liver (MASH). Say plainly that it is not approved as of Oct 2026, and give GI side effects (72.8–77.7% vs 38.6% placebo).
candidates.why_now: NEJM paper plus a Zealand release on Oct 1, Healio/AJMC coverage, and STAT calling it an 'obesity drug disappointment' on Oct 2. Creator coverage is still thin. It fits our best formula: a named drug plus a headline decoder.

evidence.signal: SYNCHRONIZE-2: n=752, T2D + BMI ≥27; −13.1% (6 mg), −10.4% (3.6 mg) vs −3.1% placebo at 76 wk
Company release: up to 13.1% weight loss, HbA1c down up to 1.21 points from 7.4%
Pharmalot frames it as an 'obesity drug disappointment' (Boehringer/Zealand)
Investigator calls the weight loss 'impressive' in T2D: opposing framings to decode

candidates.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) heart safety: non-inferior to insulin glargine for major heart events in adults with type 2 diabetes at higher cardiovascular risk (ACHIEVE-4, Lancet)
candidates.angle: 'Is the Foundayo pill safe for your heart?' The primary result is non-inferiority (MACE-4 HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.59–1.20), not superiority. HbA1c fell 1.6 vs 1.0 points; weight changed −8.8% vs +1.7% on insulin glargine. Mention the 'fewer deaths' figure (HR 0.43) only as nominal, not controlled for multiplicity, so don't call it proven. Absolute event rates must be pulled from the Lancet paper.
candidates.why_now: Lancet paper plus EASD presentation and Lilly release. Fierce Pharma says Foundayo is 'surging' and searches for the pill are rising. Most coverage so far is trade press, with few creators.

evidence.signal: Largest and longest T2D study; CV safety confirmed
MACE-4 HR 0.84 (0.59–1.20); A1C −1.6 vs −1.0; weight −8.8% vs +1.7%; all-cause death HR 0.43, nominal
ACHIEVE-4 phase 3, open-label, event-driven

candidates.topic: Trevogrumab + semaglutide: lean-mass loss 4.2% vs 7.3% on semaglutide alone over 52 weeks (Regeneron Phase 2 COURAGE, not yet peer-reviewed)
candidates.angle: 'Can a drug stop muscle loss on semaglutide (Wegovy)?' Give the numbers with the 75 mg dose, the comparator, and the fact that 25 mg wasn't significant. Say clearly that it is investigational, company-funded and not yet peer-reviewed. Then pivot to what you can do today: protein (with the kidney caveat) and strength training.
candidates.why_now: Regeneron release on Oct 1, then News-Medical, Medical Daily and medicaldialogues on Oct 3–4. 'Muscle on GLP-1' is one of our double-down topics, and Yahoo's 'surprising muscle' Wegovy story shows mainstream appetite.

Trevogrumab cuts semaglutide-induced lean mass loss by half
4.2% vs 7.3% lean mass loss at 52 wk; 25 mg not significant; not peer-reviewed

candidates.topic: Petrelintide, an amylin drug: 8.7–10.7% weight loss at 42 weeks vs 1.7% placebo at 28 weeks, nausea 20% vs 6% (ZUPREME-1, Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology)
candidates.angle: 'What is amylin, and why are Lilly and Novo betting on it after GLP-1?' Amylin is a partner hormone to GLP-1. Petrelintide gave less weight loss than semaglutide or tirzepatide but seemed gentler on the gut. The study included people without diabetes (n=485). It's Phase 2, now entering Phase 3, and not approved.
candidates.why_now: Lancet D&E paper (Sep 29), CNBC's 'why Lilly and Novo are betting on amylin' (Oct 2), and amylin combos (CagriSema, EloraTZP) in the news. Explainer search demand is building and there are very few creator videos.

evidence.signal: ZUPREME-1 phase 2 RCT published
~10% weight loss with adverse events comparable to placebo

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines and anaesthesia: regurgitation or aspiration in 1.41% of GLP-1 users vs 0.12% of non-users (UK prospective cohort, 47,039 patients, Anaesthesia)
candidates.angle: 'On semaglutide or tirzepatide and having surgery or an endoscopy? Tell your anaesthetist.' Explain the mechanism (slower gastric emptying). Give absolute rates alongside the odds ratio of 11.4. It's observational. Never advise pausing the medicine: 'follow the instructions your surgical team gives you.' Note that medical societies differ (Medscape).
candidates.why_now: HealthDay/MedicalXpress pickup on Oct 2, an earlier MedicalXpress '11-fold' headline, and Medscape's 'why can't societies agree' piece. It's a practical, high-intent search with few clear explainers.

evidence.signal: Potter et al: national prospective multicentre cohort, 119 UK sites
0.12% vs 1.41% aspiration/regurgitation; OR 11.39; mostly at emergence
GLP-1s and surgery: societies disagree on guidance

candidates.topic: Retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 now peer-reviewed in The Lancet: 23.4% average weight loss at 80 weeks on 12 mg in adults with type 2 diabetes and BMI ≥35 (efficacy estimand)
candidates.angle: Decoder: '25%? 23.4%? 20.8%? Which retatrutide number is real?' Explain the subgroup (BMI ≥35) vs the overall group (up to 20.8% vs 4.0% placebo), and the efficacy estimand vs treatment-regimen estimand. Not approved as of Oct 2026, and online 'retatrutide' isn't Lilly's trial drug.
candidates.why_now: The Lancet paper went out Sep 29, NDTV ran '25%' on Oct 3, and the BBC Woman's Hour covered it. Search queries like 'retatrutide approval status' are spiking. It's crowded, but our number-decoder angle is differentiated, and retatrutide is our proven title subject.

evidence.signal: TRIUMPH-2 phase 3 published
23.4% (60.8 lb) at 12 mg in BMI ≥35 subgroup
n=1,152 adults with T2D and BMI ≥27

candidates.topic: EloraTZP (eloralintide + tirzepatide) vs tirzepatide (Zepbound) alone: up to 23.3% weight loss in adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity (Phase 2, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Amylin + Mounjaro: what does adding a second hormone add?' Compare it with tirzepatide 15 mg in the same trial (14.8%). Make clear it's Phase 2 (n=367) at 48 weeks, years from approval. Links naturally to the petrelintide/amylin explainer.
candidates.why_now: Second snapshot at high momentum (90, 88). Endpoints calls it 'best-ever weight loss'; Pharmacy Times and Medical Daily have picked it up. Few creator videos.

candidates.topic: Semaglutide for alcohol use disorder: heavy-drinking days fell 13.7 percentage points more than placebo in adults with AUD and obesity (randomised trial, n=108)
candidates.angle: 'Does Ozempic (semaglutide) curb drinking?' Cover the brain reward system. The trial was small, only in treatment-seeking adults with moderate–severe AUD plus obesity, and semaglutide isn't approved for alcohol use. Include support resources with their real hours.
candidates.why_now: Medical Economics Morning Update on Oct 2 plus Drug Topics' 'fewer asthma attacks, lower psychiatric risk'. This is a perennial viral question and the evidence-beyond-weight pillar has a fresh RCT hook.

candidates.topic: GLP-1 prescriptions after childbirth rose 24-fold (0.08% to 1.9% of privately insured new mothers, 2018–2025, JAMA), with little breastfeeding safety data
candidates.angle: 'GLP-1 after having a baby: what we know (and don't) about breastfeeding.' Use the JAMA numbers: 1 in 6 new mothers with type 2 diabetes. Say the study didn't measure safety. Explain what the drug labels say about breastfeeding, and why to plan with your obstetrician or prescriber. No dosing, no encouraging postpartum dieting.
candidates.why_now: JAMA research letter on Oct 1, followed by US News, Yahoo and Medical Daily on Oct 2–4. Many women on GLP-1s ask about breastfeeding and there are few balanced explainers.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 use surging among new mothers (JAMA)

candidates.topic: 'Ozempic nails': nail detachment reported by 39.3% of GLP-1 users vs 8.7% of controls in a self-reported EADV survey (575 users vs 1,329 controls)
candidates.angle: Follow-up decoder for the mainstream wave: 'Can GLP-1s make your nails fall off?' It was a cross-sectional, self-reported survey. About half of users said their nail problems predated treatment, and the adjusted difference was about 2–3×, not 'four times'. Cover the possible role of rapid weight loss and nutrition, and when to see a dermatologist. Keep scope exact: the controls are the 1,329 group.
candidates.why_now: NewsNation (Oct 4), Inc.com, US News and Medical Daily, with the WaPo/ABC hair-loss genetics story running in parallel. We already covered it, so only do a myth-correcting follow-up on the inflated '4×/7×' headlines.
